angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 867,538 km at 15.04 pc = 0.77 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 66.47 +/- 0.32 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 15.044 +/- 0.072 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 66.9958 +/- 0.0921 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94), 727.0 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.247 +/- 0.021 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.771 +/- 0.012 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.247 +/- 0.021 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 867,538 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.034 +/- 0.036 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.034 +/- 0.036 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5612 +/- 52 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5612 +/- 52 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5612 +/- 52 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-86728.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.261, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
